title: The Field Brief
blurb: Daily scout surface for CR-Harness and adjacent agent-control research. Public sources only. Not an hourly Cao-style feed — refresh ~daily. Lives under CR-Harness (not hub homepage).

entries.title: STRATA: role-split LLM agents + a post-match Review Agent for Red Alert
entries.summary: Tian, Zhang et al., arXiv:2609.38881 (submitted 30 Sep 2026). Hierarchical LLM system for the RTS game Red Alert: a Strategic Agent sets high-level directives from global state plus retrieved 'experience cards', a Logistics Agent and a Tactical Agent handle logistics and tactical execution (motivated by inference latency missing tactical events). After each match a Review Agent derives candidate experience from game traces, validates/revises it with evidence from later matches, and compresses cross-game-supported lessons into cards. Reported: under a fixed scenario, using learned cards raises observed win rate from 30% to 100%. That is a single fixed scenario; abstract-level claim, I did not read the full paper.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Closest public design to a multi-agent Mini Royale player: fast tactical agent + slower strategic agent + offline reviewer that only promotes lessons validated on later matches. The validate-on-later-matches step is the part worth stealing; the headline 30%→100% is one scenario and should not be read as a general effect.

entries.title: NAQD-Env: can language agents withdraw only the affected actions?
entries.summary: Abouzahra et al., arXiv:2609.38460 (submitted 29 Sep 2026). Synthetic environment that tests whether an agent suspends affected planned actions when evidence changes, permission is revoked or a stop arrives, while preserving unaffected work and resuming only after repair. 350 frozen scenarios, 11 dependency families, three open-weight models (Qwen2.5-3B/7B, Llama-3.1-8B) under three prompts (3,150 episodes): withdrawal recall at most 0.06, no valid resumption at eligible opportunities, one episode matches the full reference policy. Exploratory SFT probes lift Qwen2.5-3B decision accuracy from 0.45–0.54 to 0.83–0.92 but show inappropriate withdrawal and lost event reporting. Small open models, synthetic structured inputs.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Gives CR a vocabulary and metric set for a case legal_actions does not cover: a queued plan (e.g., a planned push) that must be partially cancelled when the board changes. Separates attempted violations from violations the gate lets through, and reports resumption, not only withdrawal.

entries.title: Who verifies the verifier? Corrupting the committed graph defeats a causal action gate
entries.summary: Rovai, arXiv:2609.40027 (submitted 30 Sep 2026). Red-teams CIVeX, a causal action verifier that gates state-changing tool calls against a committed action-state graph and reports zero false executions on a confounded benchmark. Omitting one bidirected edge raises false executions to 15.3% (91% of executions harmful); reversing one arrowhead gives 48.9% false executions and no correct ones; every such action still carries an internally valid certificate. A randomized-sample attestation step detected both attacks (2 false alarms in 555 executions) and refusing failures gave zero false executions, but 97.1% of beneficial actions were still never executed. Costs: 127 experiments per 1,050 actions for safety, 614 more to recover the lost value.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: A whitelist is only as good as the rule/graph behind it. If the sim's legal_actions logic has a missing case, every illegal-but-allowed action will look validly certified. Argues for sampling-based attestation (replay accepted actions against the sim) and for tracking wrongful rejections, not only wrongful accepts.

entries.title: Scoping review: local-decision gains vs task-level gains in LLM agents
entries.summary: Zhang, Chang et al., arXiv:2609.39989 (submitted 30 Sep 2026). Critical scoping review of 348 studies (90 comparison records examined; 8 cases synthesized) on what evidence a component replacement in an agent establishes. Of 222 studies reporting local decision metrics, 142 also report measured task endpoints and 49 only proxies, without establishing matched comparisons. Concludes that neither online execution nor simultaneous gains in local and task metrics alone shows that better local decisions explain a task-level gain; derives eight claim-specific reporting items.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Directly about the decision_point eval question: when a gate or router improves decision-level accuracy, did match outcomes improve because of it? CR should report local decision metrics and match endpoints from the same matched runs, and log which downstream states the replacement changed.

entries.title: Multi-agent discussion gains less when dissent is withheld
entries.summary: Mansuri, Wang, Li et al., arXiv:2609.38324 (submitted 29 Sep 2026). A small model with four agent behaviors (withholding dissent, internalizing a stated answer, reconsidering after seeing dissent, correcting toward the right answer) predicts that discussion can overturn a wrong initial majority only if the withholding rate c is below c* = γ/(γ+a). Rates are estimated from conversation logs; gains shrink as withholding rises across LLMs on HiddenBench and MedEInst, instructing agents not to withhold dissent increases the gain, and turning reasoning off also increases the gain.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Third data point this week, alongside the answer-substitution and debate-collapse papers: blind first, then discuss, and prompt reviewers to state dissent explicitly. Gives a measurable quantity (withholding rate) to log in dual-LGTM transcripts.

entries.title: Upstream messages override correct answers: answer substitution in multi-agent LLMs
entries.summary: Gong, Zhang, Gao et al., arXiv:2609.36855 (submitted 29 Sep 2026). Controlled study over five benchmarks and five receivers, holding downstream task and evidence fixed and comparing no message, the upstream agent's message, and a message with the opposite conclusion. Messages often help when the receiver would otherwise be wrong, but when it would have been right an incorrect upstream message changes the answer in up to 32% of cases; in 94% of audited harmful cases the receiver copies the upstream's specific wrong answer ('answer substitution'). Removing unreliable messages recovers part of the lost accuracy.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Second independent result (after the 09-25 debate-collapse paper) that exposing a peer's verdict to a reviewer can destroy a correct independent judgement. Supports blind dual-LGTM and suggests any multi-agent CR design (planner → executor) should pass evidence, not conclusions, unless upstream reliability is known.

entries.title: Executable-contract audit: agent benchmark scores can rest on defective tools
entries.summary: Bellibatlu, Wang, Zhang et al., arXiv:2609.37315 (submitted 29 Sep 2026). Treats each tool's advertised interface as an executable contract and checks the implementation and evaluator provenance. Across 34 audited mutating tools in four benchmarks it confirms seven tool defects and one evaluator property; on injected defects the checker had no false positives in 25 flags but missed most (in 29 of 33 scored misses a clause covered the defect but no probe revealed it). Clearest case: a clinical benchmark whose tool reports writes executed under an undisclosed no-write design, so its grader scores whether a request carried the expected payload, not whether any record changed.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Direct warning for CR ETL: a score derived from what the sim says it did can be wrong if the sim does not do it. Check Mini Royale's action-result contract (accepted deploy actually changes sim state) with probes, and trace each reported metric back to state the sim wrote.

entries.title: GlyphBench: observation format and harness as measured factors in game agents
entries.summary: Castanyer, Côté et al., arXiv:2609.34214 (submitted 28 Sep 2026). 360+ game tasks rendered as 2-D Unicode glyph grids behind one train/eval/replay interface. Studies how observation interface, reasoning effort and agent harness change performance: glyph observations beat native text and pixels in their Craftax experiments, with further gains on several BALROG environments. In RL runs, invalid actions are treated as no-ops. RL on 100 GlyphBench tasks lifts Qwen3.5-4B to 63.48% on held-out Reasoning Gym vs 62.29% (math RL), 58.98% (code RL) and 56.04% base.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Mini Royale's state rendering for decision_point (text vs grid vs structured) is a harness factor, not a constant: GlyphBench shows an observation-format ablation is worth running next to the legal_actions ablation. Also a second explicit data point for 'invalid action = no-op' as a harness policy (cf. Game Arena's retry/forfeit rules).

entries.title: Kaggle Game Arena tech report: retry/forfeit harness rules as eval design
entries.summary: Doerschuk-Tiberi et al. (Kaggle + Google DeepMind), arXiv:2609.31473 (submitted 25 Sep 2026). Chess, Poker and Werewolf environments with open harness (google-deepmind/game_arena). Chess: legality enforced by the environment; an invalid move gets a bare 'invalid, retry' with diagnostics intentionally hidden, 3 retries, 4th failure = loss; retries ('rethinks') tracked as a reliability metric, and the report finds illegal moves concentrate later in games for weaker models. Poker: one retry, then defaults to check/fold; 20,000 hands per pair, 900,000 hands total, BB/100 with block bootstrap. Werewolf: parse failures past a retry cap force a turn forfeit. Per-game metrics: Bradley–Terry Elo, BB/100, game-theoretic eval.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: The most public, large-scale statement of the design choices CR must make at every decision_point: show the legal list or not, how much feedback on an illegal action, how many retries, and what the fallback is (loss vs conservative default vs forfeit). CR should declare these as a versioned harness policy and log rethink counts by match phase.

entries.title: ContrAgent: one LTLf→DFA contract gates actions online and grades traces offline
entries.summary: Xiao, Nuzzo et al., arXiv:2609.18128 (16 Sep 2026). Tool-call traces become sequences over checkable predicates; required behavior is written as assume-guarantee contracts in LTLf and compiled to a DFA used both to gate agent actions online and to evaluate recorded traces offline. On four benchmarks it matches LLM-judge and rule-based guardrail baselines with deterministic, reproducible verdicts and orders-of-magnitude lower per-call latency online.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: legal_actions covers per-step legality; temporal rules (e.g., no deploy when elixir can't cover it, no repeated rejected action N times) need a sequence check. One DFA artifact could both gate the cockpit live and score ETL logs offline, keeping online and offline verdicts identical.

entries.title: Agent UQ taxonomy + TC-ECE: step calibration ≠ trajectory calibration
entries.summary: Lin et al., arXiv:2609.07395 (7 Sep 2026). Three-axis taxonomy of agent uncertainty (what, how estimated, where in the pipeline); a counterexample shows step-level calibration does not imply trajectory-level calibration. Proposes Trajectory-Checkpoint ECE and a reporting protocol; on real traces (four models, up to 50 steps) self-reported confidence does not consistently beat a simple baseline, and pooling all trajectories can hide late-stage overconfidence.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: If CR gates decisions on confidence (Jev/REFLEX idea), calibration must be reported by match phase checkpoints, not pooled — late-match overconfidence is exactly where a pooled ECE would look fine.

entries.title: REFLEX: Jev typed-choice gate + strong-LLM fallback, measured
entries.summary: Wu & Lim (NTU), arXiv:2609.26532 (submitted 22 Sep 2026). REFLEX uses Jev (jev-1.13.0) as a typed decision layer returning (choice, confidence); execute when c≥τ and executable, else fall back to a strong LLM. Frozen 100-task REFLEX-Sim: 95% success vs 88% strong-only with 72.7% fewer strong-model calls at τ=0.5; 66–72% call reduction across Qwen3.8-Max / Kimi K3 / DeepSeek-V4-Pro fallbacks. Honest limits: on BFCL, choosing which function is 98.4% accurate but deciding whether to call any is 52.0%; on τ²-bench a cheap Flash self-escalation cascade stays competitive. Larger action sets (K 10→50) and near-valid competitors reduce accuracy.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: First public controlled evaluation of exactly the jev-gameplay-decision-router idea: typed choice over an allowed set + confidence floor + fallback. Gives CR a metric template (GMR, risk–coverage/AURC, strong calls per success, commit-vs-defer error split) and a warning that legal_actions size and near-valid alternatives degrade the gate.

entries.title: Action-class diagnostic: Acc ≤ GAR exposes act/ask/refuse miscalibration
entries.summary: Zhao et al., arXiv:2609.00949 (1 Sep 2026). Decomposes multi-turn tool-calling failures into action-class miscalibration vs execution failure over TOOL_CALL/ASK/REFUSE/CONFIRM, with an upper bound Acc ≤ Gold Action Recall. Bound violations reveal state graders that mask wrong action classes; context-only perturbations can move accuracy +11.5 vs −21.0 pp across families on the same scenario.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR decision_points also have action classes (play card / wait-noop / escalate). Logging a gold/expected class separately from the chosen action id lets ETL catch outcome graders that reward lucky wins from the wrong class of decision.

entries.title: Jev at decision_point: typed Choice/Noul gate over legal_actions
entries.summary: TypeSafe Jev (OpenRouter typesafe/jev-1.13) returns Choice/Noul/Score with probabilities — no prose. Already LIVE on the fleet harness at confidence_floor 0.55 for CoS routing. Scout ask: wire the same router into Mini Royale gameplay at decision_point (legal_actions whitelist + cockpit path), not hub routing only. Prior art: AutoHarness/PTCG legal masks, R2V residual-risk escalate, confidence-gate act/ask/abstain, HarnessBridge reject-with-feedback.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR already emits decision_point + legal_actions; Jev can Choice among legal ids or Noul-gate escalate/noop when conf<floor, with ETL logging of conf/fallback — reusable eval surface for latency vs false-escalate.

entries.title: AutoHarness: synthesize code that blocks illegal moves
entries.summary: DeepMind (Lou et al.): Gemini-2.5-Flash iteratively synthesizes an is_legal_action / propose_action code harness via Thompson-sampling tree search over environment feedback. Claims 100% legal-action rate across 145 TextArena games; smaller Flash+harness beats larger Pro on many 1P/2P evals. Direct analogue to CR-Harness legal_actions at decision_point.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR already whitelists legal_actions — AutoHarness shows how to auto-build or regression-test that verifier from env feedback, and how illegal-move rate dominates LLM game losses.

entries.title: PTCG-Bench: legal-action masking swings card-game ratings
entries.summary: Hua et al.: Pokémon TCG benchmark for LLM agents with modular harness ablations (structured obs, legal-action masking, history). Removing legal-action masking drops Glicko-2 by ~118 points and raises invalid-action rate to ~16%. Self-evolution across rounds stays unstable. Closest public TCG analogue to Mini Royale decision_points.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Quantifies how much of ‘LLM skill’ is really the mask + observation schema — exactly what CR’s legal_actions + ETL should report per model–harness pair.

entries.title: Adversarial Review: structured disagreement beats naive dual LGTM
entries.summary: Qiu & Gill (arXiv:2608.18167): reviewer + critic protocol; naive AR collapses into false consensus; three-way critic verdicts (AGREE / DISAGREE_EVIDENCE / DISAGREE_CONCERN) lift SWE-PRBench F1. Portable as SKILL.md. Maps onto fleet blind dual-LGTM (Astra + second seat).
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Fleet coding loop already wants blind dual LGTM; AR’s typed disagreement is a concrete protocol upgrade for Github Bot EM / Manage review babysitting — also useful when reviewing CR cockpit/eval PRs.

entries.title: Harness-Bench: report model–harness pairs, not models alone
entries.summary: Qihoo360 Harness-Bench (arXiv:2605.27922): 106 sandboxed agent tasks; 5194 trajectories show large variance across model–harness pairings. Flags execution-alignment failures (reasoning decoupled from tool feedback / workspace state).
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR batch evals should score (model, prompt, legal_actions schema, retry policy) as one config — not attribute wins to the LLM alone.
